clue.text: PM's son in college visiting friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: in signals the son's letter going inside the college name

parts.note: Merton is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister's boy, up at Oxford, drops in on a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' only joins the pieces: PAL comes first, then MERTON with S put inside it by 'in'. The 's of PM's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Palmerston served twice as British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Nothing to stuff in flap all around

indicators.note: in puts the nothing and stuff pieces inside the word for flap

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
O resembles zero, nothing
to ram is to cram or stuff

explanation.surface: Nothing to fill a flap on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: Panoramic describes a view covering all directions around.

clue.text: Child in top that was restricting

indicators.note: in puts the child inside the top

parts.note: a lid is a top
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A child stuffed into a confining top.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited is the past tense of limit, which means to restrict.

clue.text: I lecture dreadful old bag

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the letters of I lecture are poorly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits their talks are awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old bag' sounds like an insult; it is a literal bag of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule was a small drawstring handbag carried by women in the past.

clue.text: Give up final place, and be disturbed by later events?

parts.note: to turn in is to hand over or give up
one's grave is one's last resting place

explanation.surface: A competitor surrenders last place and is upset by what happens next.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes how a dead person would be appalled by events after their time.

clue.text: New starter without a deputy

parts.note: being without something is having no such thing
vice, as in vice-president, denotes a deputy

explanation.surface: A newcomer with nobody to deputise.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Sport with no positive result?

parts.note: a sum is the result of adding, a plus or positive operation
O, shaped like zero, stands for no or nothing

explanation.surface: A game where nobody ever comes out ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sum equal to nought: SUM then O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese wrestling sport between heavyweight competitors.

clue.text: When one is too young to use the oven?

definitions.text: When one is too young to use the oven?

parts.words: When one is too young to use the oven?
parts.note: a time of life when one only eats cold uncooked food, a youthful era

explanation.surface: Childhood, when you are not yet allowed to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, means one's inexperienced youth.

clue.text: MORI may follow this reminder as a warning

definitions.meaning: the Latin phrase meaning remember you must die

explanation.surface: A reminder that death comes for all.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir that serves to remind someone of something.

clue.text: At least that shiny? Don't mind

definitions.meaning: read as not more matt: anything that is ... is at least as glossy
the phrase said when something is of no importance, never mind

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off whether a finish is glossy enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to dismiss something as unimportant, as when one says never mind.

clue.text: Control of radio in space

definitions.meaning: the knob that sets how loud a radio plays
the amount of room something occupies

explanation.surface: Operating a radio from somewhere out in space.
explanation.definitionFit: The loudness knob is the volume control, and volume also means cubic capacity or room.

clue.text: Children not the first that were piped away

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for children is dropped

parts.note: brats are badly behaved children

explanation.surface: Recalling the children who were led off by the Pied Piper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pied Piper of Hamelin first piped the town's rats away, before the children; the surface invites you to think of the children.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend the Pied Piper lured the rodents out of Hamelin with his pipe music.

clue.text: Two pennies, perhaps, I had hidden in the same place

parts.note: a penny is a coin

indicators.note: hidden says the I had contraction is tucked away inside the second coin word

parts.note: a cent is a penny in American money
I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: Someone stashed a couple of coins in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two coins, the second an American penny; 'in' belongs to the definition, not the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincident means occupying the same space or happening at the same time.

clue.text: Exhausted by the sea, securing nothing as prize

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: securing means holding the nothing letter inside the word for worn out

parts.note: all in means worn out
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A weary sailor by the sea comes away with no award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' looks like a description of a tired sailor; it is the wordplay, and 'by' just sets the sea beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal, the kind awarded as a prize.

clue.text: Singing by turns, for real?

explanation.surface: Asking whether alternating singing is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is responsive singing by two groups in alternation.

clue.text: Disaster as bible almost pawned?

annotationWithheld.why: Disaster as bible almost pawned? (5): AV (bible) in HOC(K) (almost 'hock'); 'pawned' means 'in hock', so the one word gives both HOCK and the containment, doing two jobs

clue.text: Sort of paper that holds a lot of ink

definitions.text: that holds a lot of ink
definitions.meaning: a replaceable ink container for a printer or pen

explanation.surface: Describing paper that soaks up ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartridge paper is a heavy drawing paper, and a printer cartridge is filled with ink.

clue.text: Be ineffective, trying to dissect cubes?

definitions.meaning: to make no impression on anyone
literally slicing frozen blocks of water

explanation.surface: A futile attempt at chopping cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have no influence or effect.

clue.text: Gingham, say, large amount in check

indicators.note: in puts the large amount inside the chess abbreviation

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: A big bolt of checked fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Gingham is checked, so 'check' looks like part of the definition; it is the chess abbreviation CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is an example of a woven fabric, a cotton cloth in checks.

clue.text: Eagle in trouble, making a descent

indicators.note: trouble signals the letters of eagle in being disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird in difficulty plunges down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descent' suggests a bird coming down; it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage means line of descent, one's ancestry.

clue.text: Take aside Canterbury pilgrim?

parts.note: Canterbury is in Kent, in the south-east (SE) of England
a quester is one on a quest, as a pilgrim is

explanation.surface: Drawing aside one of Chaucer's travellers to Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the south-eastern English county containing Canterbury, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester someone is to set them apart or isolate them.

clue.text: After picking up, drop off your boy

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: to omit is to leave off or drop
thy is an old form of your

explanation.surface: Collecting and then dropping off a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is an example of a common English given name for a male child.

clue.text: Being a piece of potato short is a disaster

indicators.note: short says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a crisp is a thin fried slice of potato

explanation.surface: Being short of a crisp is a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: A crisp is what Americans call a potato chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of disaster or great danger.

clue.text: One blooming simple game: fail to finish

parts.note: snap is a basic children's card game
to drag on is to go on and on without ending

explanation.surface: A simple game that never seems to end.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAP is a card game where players shout when two matching cards turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden flower, so one that blooms.

clue.text: Ruler captured by some miracle

indicators.note: the ruler is held within the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A sovereign seized as if by a miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, a ruler.

clue.text: Terraces I put in the wrong place — language!

indicators.note: the I is moved to a different spot in the word for terraces

parts.note: patios are paved terraces

explanation.surface: Someone swears after misplacing their paving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'language!' looks like an exclamation at swearing; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional dialect, a form of language.

clue.text: Moved to platform with a song about ghost, not too big

indicators.note: about says the song goes round the shortened ghost

parts.note: a lied is a German art song

indicators.note: not says the outsize letters are removed from the ghost word

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, too big

explanation.surface: A singer steps onto a stage with a ghostly ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes OS (outsize, too big) out of GHOST, leaving GHT, and 'about' puts the song round that.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get down from a train or vehicle, as onto a platform.

clue.text: Tips of stone axes are hot

indicators.note: the first and last letters of stone are taken

parts.note: X and Y are the two axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Flint hand-axes with sharp, burning edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips of' applies only to stone; the axes are the graph's X and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for sexually attractive.

clue.text: Pigeonhole hi-fi fan?

definitions.meaning: humorously, the sort of person who loves a sound system

explanation.surface: Labelling someone as an audio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: To stereotype is to pigeonhole someone by a fixed, simplified idea.
